blocks.text: Mir Mannu responds to repeated Sikh raids near Lahore's outskirts by deciding that ordinary policing is no longer enough and that the Khalsa must be rooted out completely. Orders go out across the province to seize or kill Singhs wherever they can be found, turning his administration into an instrument of systematic persecution.

The pressure becomes so severe that whole Sikh families lose safe refuge in Majha and depend on scattered sympathizers for survival. One important hiding place is Pandori in the Majha area, where the household associated with saint Dadu Ram shelters vulnerable women connected to the Sikh community.

When informers expose the arrangement, Mir Mannu's men descend on the site, arrest the grandson of saint Dadu Ram, and search the monastery for fugitives. The women escape immediate discovery only by taking on the red robes of that sect, a detail that underscores both the danger and the ingenuity of those being hunted.
